title: Gulveer Singh Creates History With India's First Commonwealth Games 10,000m Medal
excerpt: The Army runner won silver in Glasgow while weightlifter Harjinder Kaur also claimed silver and two boxers guaranteed medals on a productive Day 5.
body:
• Gulveer Singh won silver in the men's 10,000m, becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the event.
  • Weightlifter Harjinder Kaur clinched silver in the women's 69kg with a career-best 227kg total.
  • Boxers Preeti Pawar and Priya Ghanghas reached the semi-finals, guaranteeing at least bronze medals.
  • India's medal tally at CWG 2026 reached 10 after Day 5, with golds from Mirabai Chanu and Sharmila Dhankar anchoring the count.

A Historic Night on the Track

Gulveer Singh etched his name into Indian athletics history at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium on Monday night, winning silver in the men's 10,000m final to become the first Indian to medal in the event at the Commonwealth Games.

"Long-distance running has historically been a weak spot for India at the Commonwealth Games."

The 28-year-old Army runner, who has spent the last two seasons rewriting India's distance-running record books, entered Glasgow in career-best form. He became the first Indian to dip under 13 minutes in the 5,000m last year, smashed the national 10,000m record with 27:00.22, and earlier this year became the first Indian to run a sub-four-minute mile.

Long-distance running has historically been a weak spot for India at the Commonwealth Games. Gulveer's silver shatters that narrative and signals a generational shift in the country's athletics programme.

Harjinder Kaur Delivers on the Platform

In the weightlifting arena at the SEC Armadillo, Harjinder Kaur added another silver to India's growing tally in the women's 69kg category. The Birmingham 2022 bronze medallist lifted a career-best combined total of 227kg, improving on her previous Commonwealth Games performance.

Harjinder's silver extends India's remarkable run on the weightlifting platform in Glasgow, where Mirabai Chanu's historic hat-trick gold, Rishikanta Singh's silver, Muthupandi Raja's silver, Gyaneshwari Yadav's silver, and Bindyarani Devi's bronze have made weightlifting India's most prolific medal sport at these Games.

Boxing Guarantees More Hardware

In the boxing ring, Preeti Pawar and Priya Ghanghas both won their quarter-final bouts to advance to the semi-finals, guaranteeing at least bronze medals. Jadumani Mandengbam also reached the semi-finals after defeating Zambia's Mwale, adding another assured medal to India's boxing haul.

Medal Count and What's Ahead

India's medal tally stands at 10 after Day 5 — one gold (Mirabai Chanu in 48kg weightlifting), six silvers, and three bronzes across weightlifting, athletics, and para-athletics. Swimming offered a mixed bag: Srihari Nataraj advanced to the 100m backstroke semi-finals, while Sajan Prakash was eliminated in the 50m butterfly heats.

Day 6 promises more medal action with Gulveer Singh also entered in the 5,000m, where he could attempt a rare distance double. The athletics programme continues to gather pace with more Indian athletes entering medal rounds across field and track events.
